title: Container Image Signing & Verification Playbook — On‑Prem Packaging
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the recommended process, tooling, and operational checks for signing, attesting, and verifying container images and associated artifacts before delivering on‑premise packages to customers or deploying into VPC/private clusters. It is intended for release engineers, private‑deploy delivery leads, security engineers, and SREs who manage packaging and day‑2 validation for air‑gapped or VPC‑connected environments.

Goals

- Ensure strong end‑to‑end integrity guarantees for on‑prem images and runtime artifacts.
- Produce verifiable audit artifacts (signatures, SBOMs, provenance) suitable for customer evidence and compliance.
- Provide a reproducible, automatable workflow that works in air‑gapped and partially connected environments.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to all on‑prem packages and customer images produced by Redwood build pipelines (control plane, runtime containers, bootstrap artifacts).
- Assumes build infrastructure can produce SBOMs and deterministic builds (best effort).
- Air‑gapped customers: rely on offline signing workflows and transported attestations (Rekor bundles / OIDCless verification).

Key definitions

- Signature: cryptographic signature over a container image manifest (cosign, notary v2).
- SBOM: Software Bill of Materials (CycloneDX/JSON or SPDX) describing package contents.
- Attestation: higher‑level metadata about build provenance (SLSA level, build id, source repo commit).
- Transparency log: public or private ledger (e.g., Rekor) used to store signed artifact entries for non‑repudiation.

Roles & ownership

- Release Engineers: produce signed images, SBOMs, and attestations. Primary owners of build keys.
- Private Deploy Delivery Lead: coordinate distribution and validation with customer ops.
- Security (Supply‑Chain): define signing policy, rotate KMS/HSM keys, audit logs quarterly.
- SRE / Day‑2 Ops: verify signatures during installation and on upgrades; run periodic re‑validation jobs.

High‑level process (summary)

1) Build: produce deterministic image + SBOM + provenance metadata.
2) Sign: sign image manifest and attestation using KMS/HSM-backed keys; record entry in transparency log.
3) Export bundle: produce a delivery bundle containing image, signature, SBOM, and a signed attestation bundle (for air‑gap use cases).
4) Verify at install: customer or Redwood agent re‑validates signatures, attestations, and SBOM policy before runtime.
5) Monitor and rotate: key rotation schedule, transparency log monitoring, and incident procedures.

Detailed procedures

A. Build pipeline requirements

- Build servers must emit: image manifest digest (sha256), SBOM (CycloneDX v1.4 JSON preferred), build provenance (repo, commit, build id, timestamp), and reproducible build recipe where possible.
- CI job example (high level):

1. Checkout repository at tag/commit.
2. Run docker buildx with fixed builder and build args to reduce non‑determinism.
3. Generate SBOM with syft: `syft packages:docker:myapp:latest -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json`.
4. Produce provenance file (provenance.json) following in‑house schema.

B. Signing & attestation (connected mode)

Recommended stack: cosign (sigstore), Rekor (transparency), and optional Notary v2 for registries that support OCI signatures. For customers with Redwood KMS (hosted/dedicated), we use HSM‑backed keys.

Example cosign flow (connected):

- Generate or import key to KMS/HSM (owner: Security).
- cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/release/cryptoKeys/release-key my-registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.2.3
- cosign attest --key ksm://... --predicate provenance.json my-registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.2.3
- Rekor record is written automatically (or via `cosign upload`).

C. Signing & attestation (air‑gapped / offline)

Air‑gapped customers cannot reach Rekor or the hosted KMS. For these we follow an offline‑first workflow:

1. Build produces image tar (docker save / oras), SBOM, and provenance.
2. Offline signing appliance (controlled environment in Redwood datacenter) signs the image manifest and emits: signature.sig, attestation.json, sbom.json, and rekor_bundle.tgz (if using a Rekor mirror).
3. All artifacts are packaged into a signed transport bundle: `bundle.tar.gz` and hashed (sha256). Bundle delivered via secure courier or customer upload to a validated endpoint.

Notes: Keys used to sign offline bundles are HSM keys with strict custody; operations require 2‑person approval (ASM/CSM signoff).

D. Verification at install / runtime

Verification must be automated in the installer (customer side or Redwood delivery agent). The installer performs:

1. Verify bundle integrity: compare sha256 of delivered bundle against courier manifest or signed stamp.
2. Verify signature: `cosign verify --key ksm://... --certificate bundle/signature.pem registry/image@sha256:...` (or verify using local public key for air‑gapped).
3. Verify attestation: check provenance fields (commit matches release tag, build timestamp within expected window, builder id allowed).
4. SBOM policy checks: ensure no disallowed packages or CVEs above configured severity. Use grype or sbom‑policy tool.

Failure modes & remediation

- Signature missing or invalid: halt installation, create incident, and contact Release Engineers. Do not proceed.
- SBOM contains prohibited dependency: escalate to Product Security for triage; may require a rebuild.
- Bundle checksum mismatch: assume tampering or transport error; request re‑delivery and perform chain‑of‑custody review.
- Rekor transparency mismatch (connected): if Rekor entry absent for signed artifact, mark for manual review and quarantine.

Operational controls & SLOs

- Verification time SLO (installer verification step): 95th percentile < 6s for connected verification against a local CA/OCSP; in air‑gapped mode target < 30s for local file checks (signature + SBOM scan).
- Key rotation window: rotate release signing keys annually; emergency rotation within 24h of a suspected key compromise.
- Auditable evidence retention: retain signature attestations, SBOMs, and Rekor bundles for 3 years (customer agreement dependent).

Example acceptance test matrix

| Test case | Input | Expected result | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Valid connected signing | image:1.2.3 signed with KMS key | cosign verify passes; Rekor entry exists | Release Eng |
| Offline bundle verification | bundle.tar.gz delivered via courier | sha256 matches; signature verified with public key | Delivery Lead |
| SBOM policy violation | image with vulns above threshold | installer fails with policy error | Security |
| Tampered bundle | modified bundle | checksum mismatch; install aborted | Delivery Lead |
Note: Above table is presented as a plain text table; CI harness converts to structured test cases.

Tooling examples & snippets

- Generate SBOM (syft):
```
syft my-registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.2.3 -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
```
- Sign image (cosign, KMS URI pattern):
```
cosign sign --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/release/cryptoKeys/release-key my-registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.2.3
```
- Attest with provenance:
```
cosign attest --type swagger --key ksm://... --predicate provenance.json my-registry.example.com/redwood/runtime:1.2.3
```
- Verify offline bundle (example script outline):
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
BUNDLE=$1
SHA_EXPECTED=$2
sha256sum -c <<< "$SHA_EXPECTED  $BUNDLE"
mkdir /tmp/bundle && tar -xzvf $BUNDLE -C /tmp/bundle
cosign verify --key /etc/release/public.pem /tmp/bundle/image.tar
# verify SBOM policy
grype sbom:/tmp/bundle/sbom.json -o json | jq '.matches | length' | grep -q 0
```

Key management & custody

- Hosted/Dedicated customers: use KMS with HSM protection; Security rotates keys and maintains access logs.
- On‑prem or air‑gapped: we use dual custody for private signing keys (one key remains in Redwood HSM, the offline signing appliance uses ephemeral sub‑keys).
- Access control: least privilege; signing operations logged and require MFA + approved CI identity.

Auditing & evidence collection

- Each release must publish: image digest, SBOM, provenance.json, signature artifacts, and Rekor bundle (if available).
- Delivery artifacts stored in the internal release artifact store with ACLs and retention policy.
- Quarterly audit: Security verifies sample releases end‑to‑end (keys, Rekor entries, bundle integrity).

Rollout checklist for adopting playbook

1. Align release pipeline to emit SBOM & provenance (owner: Release Eng).
2. Configure cosign + Rekor for connected flows; validate against test registry (owner: Security).
3. Define offline bundle format and courier process for air‑gapped customers (owner: Delivery).
4. Integrate verification steps into installers/agents and CI smoke tests (owner: SRE/Delivery).
5. Run pilot with one customer and collect evidence for audit (owner: Delivery + Security).

Appendix A — Bundle layout (recommended)

- bundle.tar.gz/
  - image.tar (OCI image or docker save)
  - image.sha256 (digest file)
  - signature.sig (cms or cosign generated signature)
  - public_key.pem (public verification key for the signing key)
  - sbom.json (CycloneDX)
  - provenance.json (build metadata)
  - rekor_bundle.tgz (optional, Rekor transparency snapshot)
  - delivery-manifest.yaml (courier manifest with hashes and chain of custody)

Appendix B — Common questions

Q: Why both SBOM and attestation?
A: SBOM enumerates components and licenses; attestation conveys build provenance and policy decisions (who built, where, and which CI job). Both are required for compliance and root cause.

Q: Can customers bring their own verification keys?
A: Yes. Customer verification workflows should accept customer public keys or allow Redwood to register customer trust anchors in advance. Document the process in the customer onboarding readout.

References

- Sigstore / Cosign docs: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/
- SLSA: https://slsa.dev/
- Syft & Grype: https://github.com/anchore/syft and https://github.com/anchore/grype
- Recommended internal pages: /eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026
